x: Don Stroud ran well to finish 56th and others who performed satisfactorily were S.Boreham,C.Shippen, J.Dooley and M.Robinson. Don McLean came all the way from Oxford by motor-cycle to finish 324th - perhaps the cold got into his bones, or is there some other reason for these continuous lapses from his real form?

Stan Vickers won the latter from scratch in the fastest time to date of 21 m.46·4s. while the 2 miles was won by S.Boreham for the third year in succession - he can truly be described as the handicapper's nightmare.

At Bexley we finished only one complete team out of three just because the following failed to write or phone me despite sufficient warning :- R.Linstead, S.Charlton, S.Boreham, G.Lines, D.Manning and R.Braine.

Special mention must be made of S.Boreham, who, recovering from a bad cold reluctantly competed in the mile, finishing 3rd in 4m47s. and having been persuaded to start in the two miles to complete our team, hung on to the end, finishing in a state of collapse.
Our visitors provided the winner of the 880 yds, Steve Boreham being a good second in 2m.3.2s.; he was just unable to get on terms with the winner despite his characteristic final burst.
Simultaneously I saw Steve Boreham sink entirely and as he came up (I didn't think he could swim) I grabbed him as he was being carried away and just dumped him clear of the water on the other side.
